title: Chapter 5: Tripura — Rivers, Lakes and Climate

blocks.content: Tripura is drained by numerous rivers, most of which originate within the state's hills and flow westward into Bangladesh, ultimately joining the Padma (Ganga) and Meghna river systems. The rivers are short but significant for irrigation, power generation, and transport. Flooding is a recurring problem during monsoon.

cells: Longest river in Tripura (~160 km); Dumbur Hydroelectric Project on it; Dumbur Lake; used for irrigation
Flows through Agartala city; polluted but important
Khowai town on its banks; seasonal flooding
Important for North Tripura irrigation; tea gardens on its banks
Flows past Udaipur; Tripura Sundari Deo River
Forms boundary with Bangladesh at some points

blocks.content: Dumbur Lake, also called Loktak Lake of Northeast (though the real Loktak is in Manipur), is the largest lake/reservoir in Tripura. It is actually the reservoir created by the Gumti Hydroelectric Project (Dumbur HEP) on the Gumti River in Dhalai district. The lake is dotted with 48 small islands and is surrounded by dense jungle. It is a major tourist destination and has significant ecological importance.

items: Area: Approximately 41 sq km when full
Situated in Dhalai district; accessible from Ambassa
48 islands make it a unique landscape — some inhabited by tribal communities
Water sports: Boating, speedboat rides offered
The Dumbur Hydroelectric Project (40 MW) is located here
Natural freshwater lake in South Tripura district near Udaipur
Famous for the Neermahal — the Water Palace of the Manikya kings — built in the middle of the lake
Neermahal was constructed by Maharaja Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya Bahadur in 1930; a unique Mughal-Hindu architectural style palace on water; only floating palace in northeast India
Area: ~5 sq km; attracts migratory birds in winter
Important tourist destination; boat ride to Neermahal

blocks.content: Tripura has a humid tropical climate with heavy rainfall, high humidity, and moderate temperatures. The climate is heavily influenced by the SW Monsoon from the Bay of Bengal.

cells: Hot and humid; occasional thunderstorms (Nor'westers); high humidity
Very heavy rainfall; 2,000–2,500 mm in this period; floods common; cloudy
Retreating monsoon; pleasant; less rain; harvest season
Cool and dry; fog in valleys; minimum can reach 7–8°C in Jampui Hills; pleasant for tourism

items: Average Annual Rainfall: 2,000–2,500 mm (varies; west is drier, east and north are wetter)
Jampui Hills: Cooler and wetter; pleasant even in summer; temperature rarely exceeds 25°C
Humidity: Very high (70–90%) for most of the year
Cyclones: Bay of Bengal cyclones occasionally affect Tripura; pre-monsoon storms
